source_refs.note: Book p. 287: 11.1.2 Vector-Valued Function, r(t) = <f(t), g(t), h(t)> = f(t) i + g(t) j + h(t) k

blocks.text: Pichle page par humne dekha ke scalar function ek number deta hai. Ab sawal yeh hai: agar humein kisi cheez ki position chahiye, jis ke liye \(x\), \(y\) (aur 3D mein \(z\)) teenon chahiye, to kya karein? Jawab hai: teen scalar functions ko ek saath jor kar ek vector bana lein. Isi ko vector-valued function kehte hain.

Kitab ki definition: ek variable wala vector-valued function woh function hai jo input mein ek variable leta hai aur output mein ek vector deta hai. Output vector ka har component (hissa) khud input ka ek scalar function hota hai. Aam tor par vector-valued function aise likha jata hai:

blocks.latex: \begin{aligned}\mathbf{r}(t) &= \langle f(t), g(t), h(t)\rangle \\ &= f(t)\hat{i} + g(t)\hat{j} + h(t)\hat{k}\end{aligned}
blocks.text_alt: r of t equals the ordered triple f of t, g of t, h of t, which equals f of t times i plus g of t times j plus h of t times k

blocks.text: Yahan \(\hat{i}, \hat{j}, \hat{k}\) rectangular coordinates (\(x\), \(y\), \(z\) axes) ke unit vectors hain, aur \(f(t)\), \(g(t)\), \(h(t)\) variable \(t\) ke scalar functions hain jo vector-valued function \(\mathbf{r}(t)\) ke components hain. Yaani \(f(t)\) batata hai ke \(x\)-simt mein kitna, \(g(t)\) batata hai \(y\)-simt mein kitna, aur \(h(t)\) batata hai \(z\)-simt mein kitna.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Dono tareeqe ek hi baat kehte hain. \(\langle f(t), g(t), h(t)\rangle\) mein teenon components tarteeb se likhe hain (pehle \(x\), phir \(y\), phir \(z\)); \(f(t)\hat{i} + g(t)\hat{j} + h(t)\hat{k}\) mein har component apne unit vector ke saath likha hai. Exam mein jo form sawal mein ho, wahi istemal karein.
2D mein \(\hat{k}\) wala hissa nahin hota: \(\mathbf{r}(t) = \langle f(t), g(t)\rangle = f(t)\hat{i} + g(t)\hat{j}\).
Sab se zaroori lafz hai "single variable": tamam components ek hi \(t\) par depend karte hain. \(t\) ki ek value rakhte hi teenon components ek saath tay ho jate hain, aur ek vector mil jata hai. Is ko aise samjhiye: ek ghari (watch) ka time dekh kar aap bata sakte hain ke ghanton wali sui kahan hai aur minute wali kahan; ek hi input, kai maloomat.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Hamari taraf se misaal: Introduction wala \(\mathbf{r}(t) = t\hat{i} + t^{2}\hat{j}\) lijiye. Is ke components \(f(t) = t\) aur \(g(t) = t^{2}\) hain, yani do scalar functions. \(t = 3\) par:
\[\mathbf{r}(3) = 3\hat{i} + 9\hat{j} = \langle 3, 9\rangle\]
Ek number andar gaya (\(3\)), ek vector bahar aaya (\(\langle 3, 9\rangle\)).
Dilchasp baat: vector ki lambai \(|\mathbf{r}(t)| = \sqrt{t^{2} + t^{4}}\) phir se ek scalar function hai, kyun ke lambai sirf ek number hoti hai.
Ab dono qism ke functions ko saath saath rakh kar dekhte hain, taa ke farq hamesha ke liye yaad ho jaye:

rows: Saada harf se likha jata hai: \(f(t)\)
Tasveer: \(\mathbf{r}(t)\) ki nok ka banaya hua raasta
blocks.caption: Hamara muqabla: scalar function aur vector-valued function

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Khud sochiye: \(\mathbf{u}(t) = \langle \sin t, 5\rangle\) vector function hai? Haan: ek input \(t\), output do components wala vector. Doosra component \(5\) constant hai, magar constant bhi ek (bohat saada) scalar function hai.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Vector-valued function ek variable \(t\) leta hai aur ek vector deta hai.
2. Har component \(f(t), g(t), h(t)\) usi \(t\) ka scalar function hai.
3. \(\mathbf{r}(t) = \langle f(t), g(t), h(t)\rangle = f(t)\hat{i} + g(t)\hat{j} + h(t)\hat{k}\); 2D mein \(\hat{k}\) wala hissa nahin.
4. \(\hat{i}, \hat{j}, \hat{k}\) \(x\)-, \(y\)- aur \(z\)-axis ki simt ke unit vectors hain.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Components ko jama kar dena: \(\langle t, t^{2}\rangle\) ek vector hai, number \(t + t^{2}\) nahin.
2. Tarteeb badal dena: \(\langle f, g, h\rangle\) ka matlab hamesha pehle \(x\), phir \(y\), phir \(z\).
3. Alag components mein alag variables (ek mein \(t\), doosre mein \(s\)) likh dena: sab components ka input ek hi \(t\) hai.
